title: Abelian sheaf cohomology on directed inverse limits of spectral spaces
statement: Let $I$ be a directed set (nonempty, every pair has a common upper bound). Let $X_i$ be spectral spaces [def-weil-spectral-space], with continuous transition maps $f_{ij}:X_j\to X_i$ for $i\le j$, satisfying $f_{ii}=\mathrm{id}$ and $f_{ij}f_{jk}=f_{ik}$. Assume each $f_{ij}$ is spectral, meaning that the inverse image of every quasi-compact open is quasi-compact. Let $X$ be spectral and let continuous maps $p_i:X\to X_i$, satisfying $f_{ij}\circ p_j=p_i$ for $i\le j$, exhibit $X$ as the inverse limit in topological spaces: the map $x\mapsto(p_i(x))_i$ is a bijection onto the compatible tuples and the topology is the coarsest making all $p_i$ continuous. For each $i$ let $F_i$ be a sheaf of abelian groups on $X_i$. Give morphisms $\alpha_{ij}:F_i\to(f_{ij})_*F_j$ for $i\le j$, with $\alpha_{ii}=\mathrm{id}$ and $\alpha_{ik}=(f_{ij})_*\alpha_{jk}\circ\alpha_{ij}$, using the sectionwise equality $(f_{ik})_*=(f_{ij})_*(f_{jk})_*$ [def-weil-pbc-topological-inverse-image]. Equivalently their adjoints are compatible inverse-image maps $f_{ij}^{-1}F_i\to F_j$. On $X$ form $F=\varinjlim_{i\in I}p_i^{-1}F_i$ in abelian sheaves [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], with transition maps obtained by pulling back those adjoints and using $p_i=f_{ij}p_j$. Then for every $q\ge0$ the canonical pullback-and-coprojection maps induce an isomorphism of abelian groups $$\varinjlim_{i\in I}H^q(X_i,F_i)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^q(X,F).$$ Here cohomology is the right-derived global sections of abelian sheaves [def-sc-topological-abelian-cohomology], and the transition maps on cohomology are induced by $\alpha_{ij}$ and pullback along $f_{ij}$.

source.place: Tag 0A37, label lemma-colimit, final sentence and preceding setup, specialized to a directed-set index

proof.text: The spectral inverse-limit theorem gives spectral projections, so each $p_i^{-1}(U_i)$ is quasi-compact when $U_i$ is. The limit topology has a basis of finite intersections of inverse images of opens. Refine each stage open by its quasi-compact-open basis. For finitely many resulting opens choose a common upper index $k$; their intersection is $p_k^{-1}(\bigcap_l f_{i_lk}^{-1}U_{i_l})$, whose stage open is quasi-compact by spectrality and quasi-separatedness. Thus these inverse images form a basis. The descent-opens lemma represents every quasi-compact open at a stage and detects inclusions and finite covering equalities at later stages, as needed below.

source.place: Tag 0A30, label lemma-descend-opens; Tag 0A2Z, spectral inverse-limit basis

proof.text: Apply the section comparison to the compatible sheaf system on X. It identifies sections of F over p_i^{-1}(U_i) with the filtered colimit of the sections of F_j over f_{ij}^{-1}(U_i), and the comparison is the canonical one induced by the transition maps.

Use the full site of open subsets of each X_i with arbitrary open coverings, not a finite-cover colimit site. Its objects and inclusion morphisms form sets; unions of open covers and intersections verify the site axioms. Choose embeddings e_k:F_k\to A_k with A_k injective using enough injectives on this site. Define G_i(V)=\prod_{k\ge i}A_k(f_{ik}^{-1}V), with componentwise restrictions. This is a sheaf: a compatible local family glues uniquely in each factor, and those gluings give the unique product section. It is the product of the sheaves (f_{ik})_*A_k, with its universal property verified componentwise. Each factor is injective by the topological pushforward-injective lemma, which assumes only continuity; the product-injectives lemma gives injectivity of G_i.

source.place: Tag 0A37, label lemma-colimit, compatible injective construction and dimension shifting

proof.text: Define \gamma_i:F_i\to G_i by its k-component (f_{ik})_*e_k\circ\alpha_{ik}. Its i-component is e_i because \alpha_{ii}=1, so \gamma_i is monic. Define \beta_{ij}:G_i\to(f_{ij})_*G_j on an open V by discarding coordinates k not \ge j; the retained k-coordinate lies in A_k(f_{jk}^{-1}f_{ij}^{-1}V)=A_k(f_{ik}^{-1}V). Thus \beta_{ii}=1, and both \beta_{ik} and (f_{ij})_*\beta_{jk}\circ\beta_{ij} retain exactly the coordinates l\ge k. On coordinate k\ge j, (f_{ij})_*\gamma_j\circ\alpha_{ij} equals (f_{ik})_*e_k\circ(f_{ij})_*\alpha_{jk}\circ\alpha_{ij}=(f_{ik})_*e_k\circ\alpha_{ik}, the same as \beta_{ij}\circ\gamma_i. These are sheaf maps since coordinate projections commute with restrictions. Take adjoints to obtain the required compatible inverse-image system of injectives. This proves the construction here rather than applying the finite-cover-site system lemma.

source.place: Tag 0A37, label lemma-colimit, compatible injective construction and dimension shifting

proof.text: Let Q_i=\operatorname{coker}(\gamma_i). The exactness clause of the topological pushforward-injective lemma says that inverse image along every continuous f_{ij} and p_i is exact. The compatible maps from the preceding step therefore induce maps f_{ij}^{-1}Q_i\to Q_j by the cokernel universal property; their identity and composition laws follow by precomposing the epimorphisms f_{ij}^{-1}G_i\to f_{ij}^{-1}Q_i. Pulling back 0\to F_i\to G_i\to Q_i\to0 along p_i remains exact. Applying exact filtered colimits on the full open-set site of X gives 0\to F\to G\to Q\to0, where G=\varinjlim_i p_i^{-1}G_i and Q=\varinjlim_i p_i^{-1}Q_i. No finite-cover hypothesis is used in either cited exactness statement.

source.place: Tag 0A37, label lemma-colimit, compatible injective construction and dimension shifting

proof.text: Let B be the quasi-compact opens of X and Cov all finite coverings of members of B by members of B. They are cofinal among arbitrary open coverings: refine each covering by the quasi-compact-open basis and extract a finite subcover using quasi-compactness of the target. Finite intersections remain in B by spectrality. Descend a finite covering U=\bigcup_l U_l and its members to one stage using the open-descent lemma; the finite-stage equality is eventually a covering equality. For every later stage the pulled-back covering is still a covering and its finite intersections are quasi-compact since the transition maps are spectral. Step 2 applied to the G_i identifies each term of the ordered Cech complex with its filtered-colimit counterpart. In each fixed degree there are only finitely many tuples: a tuple of finitely many colimit sections is represented at a common stage, and equality is also detected at a common stage, so finite products commute with this colimit. Restrictions are the same under these identifications, hence so are the alternating differentials. The finite-stage complexes have zero positive cohomology by the topological injective-Cech lemma, and exact filtered colimits of abelian groups preserve this exactness. The site Cech-vanishing criterion now applies on the full open-set site, with B and Cov as above, and gives H^p(U,G)=0 for every U in B and p>0, in particular for U=X.

source.place: Tag 0A37, lemma-colimit, final proof paragraph using Tags 0A30, 01EP and 01EW

proof.text: Prove comparison in degree q for every compatible sheaf system by induction on q. Degree zero is Step 2 with U_i=X_i. For a system F_i embed it in the compatible G_i and form Q_i as in Steps 3-5. On every stage H^p(X_i,G_i)=0 for p>0 by injectivity, and on X H^p(X,G)=0 for p>0 by Step 6. Taking filtered colimits of the stage long exact sequences remains exact. To justify connecting squares also across different spaces, for any continuous $h:Y\to Z$ consider the functors $E\mapsto H^n(Y,h^{-1}E)$ on abelian sheaves of $Z$. Exactness of $h^{-1}$ and the natural long exact sequence on $Y$ make these a delta-functor. The degree-zero pullback of sections extends uniquely from the universal delta-functor $H^n(Z,-)$ to this delta-functor. Consequently these pullback maps commute with connecting maps. Composing with the maps induced by the sheaf-system morphisms, which commute with connecting maps by ordinary naturality, proves the required squares for $f_{ij}$ and $p_i$. Uniqueness of the extensions also proves compatibility with compositions, since the extensions agree in degree zero. Taking colimits preserves these commutative squares. For q=1 the two groups are cokernels of H^0(G)\to H^0(Q), identified by the degree-zero comparison for G_i and Q_i. For q>1 their connecting maps identify degree q for F with degree q-1 for Q on both sides, and the induction hypothesis for the entire quotient system Q_i gives the isomorphism. The commutative connecting squares identify these isomorphisms with the stipulated canonical pullback-and-coprojection maps.

source.place: Tag 0A37, lemma-colimit, induction and long exact sequence argument
